detail.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Adds `moe_combine_reduce_in_activation_dtype` (default off), which lets the alltoall dispatcher's expert-TP reduce-scatter in the token combine run in bf16 instead of the FP32 router dtype when the expert-TP group has exactly two ranks. In that case the result is bit-identical, and the change removes an FP32 copy of every token-expert row.

:warning: For major changes (either in lines of code or in its impact), please make sure to first share a design doc with the team. If you're unsure what's the best way to do so, contact @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall.

## Why the upcast costs memory

`MoEAlltoAllTokenDispatcher.combine_preprocess` reduce-scatters expert outputs across the expert-tensor-parallel group as

```python
reduce_scatter_to_sequence_parallel_region(
    hidden_states.to(self.probs.dtype), group=self.tp_group, ...
).to(hidden_states.dtype)
```

With `moe_router_dtype='fp32'`, `self.probs` is FP32, so this allocates an FP32 copy of every token-expert row this rank received, and the collective sends twice the bytes of the bf16 tensor. At long context this copy is the largest single allocation in the MoE layer. In SkyRL, on GLM-5.3-Flash (TP8, EP32 x ETP2), it was 19.31 GiB/GPU at 576k tokens, the allocation that ran that length out of memory.

The upcast exists so that the cross-rank sum does not round to bf16 at every step. That only matters when there is more than one step:

- **2 ranks:** each output element is one addition, `a + b`. NCCL's Ring and PAT kernels compute a bf16 sum by accumulating in FP32 and rounding once, so `reduce_scatter(bf16)` gives the same result as `reduce_scatter(fp32).to(bf16)`.
- **More than 2 ranks:** Ring adds partial sums hop by hop, and a bf16 reduction rounds after each hop. That differs from the FP32 path, so the upcast is kept.
- **NVLS:** the reduction happens inside the NVSwitch with different rounding. A forced `NCCL_ALGO=NVLS` bf16 reduce-scatter differs from the FP32 path in roughly 10-20% of elements, by at most 1 bf16 ulp. The upcast is kept whenever `NCCL_ALGO` asks for NVLS.

## Change

- `TransformerConfig.moe_combine_reduce_in_activation_dtype: bool = False`. The CLI flag `--moe-combine-reduce-in-activation-dtype` is generated from the config field.
- `MoEAlltoAllTokenDispatcher._tp_reduce_dtype(hidden_states)` returns the activation dtype when the flag is set, `self.tp_size == 2`, and `NCCL_ALGO` does not ask for NVLS. In every other case it returns `self.probs.dtype`, which is today's behavior. `combine_preprocess` calls it in place of `self.probs.dtype`. Nothing else in the method changes.
- `_nccl_algo_may_use_nvls()` matches `NCCL_ALGO` values that contain `nvls` (for example `NVLS`, `Ring,NVLS`, `reducescatter:nvls`), and does not match the exclusion form `^NVLS`.
- One row added to the Token Dispatching table in `megatron/core/transformer/moe/README.md`.

With the flag off, the code path is unchanged.

## Alternatives considered

- **Always reduce in the activation dtype.** Not exact for expert-TP groups larger than 2, and not exact under NVLS, so it would change numerics for those configurations.
- **Chunk the upcast and reduce-scatter.** This bounds the FP32 peak, but every byte is still sent in FP32 and the code gets more complex, even though for 2 ranks the FP32 path buys no accuracy.
- **Ask NCCL which algorithm it will pick.** PyTorch does not expose NCCL's per-collective algorithm choice, so the guard reads the `NCCL_ALGO` that the user set. With `NCCL_ALGO` unset, a 2-rank reduce-scatter selected Ring at every size from 1 KiB to 1 GiB in SkyRL's measurements (NCCL 2.29.7, B200).
- **Enable by default.** The result is bit-identical under Ring/PAT, but that depends on NCCL's reduction kernels, so this PR leaves the flag off. Reviewers may prefer it on.

The allgather dispatcher's `token_combine` has the same upcast pattern over the `tp_ep` group. It is out of scope here.

## Validation (from SkyRL)

The same change has been running in SkyRL as a monkeypatch, [NovaSky-AI/SkyRL#2414](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/pull/2414) (split out of [#2341](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/pull/2341)):

- **Exactness:** 2-rank bf16 reduce-scatter compared with the FP32 reduce-scatter cast back to bf16: 0 of 64M elements differ (Ring/PAT). The SkyRL patch notes record that the bit-for-bit check passed on up to 512M elements spanning five orders of magnitude, within a node and across nodes (NCCL 2.29.7, B200).
- **Memory:** On full GLM-5.3-Flash at 512k context (64 B200, ETP2), the FP32 combine ran out of memory and the bf16 combine fit at 144 GiB. At 576k tokens (TP8, EP32 x ETP2), the FP32 copy this removes was 19.31 GiB/GPU.

## Test plan

- New `tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_combine_reduce_dtype.py`:
  - `TestTpReduceDtype` (CPU): dtype decision for flag off/on, expert-TP sizes 2/4/8, bf16 and fp16 activations, and `NCCL_ALGO` values (`NVLS`, `nvls`, `Ring,NVLS`, `reducescatter:nvls`, `^NVLS`, `Ring`, `PAT`). It also checks that `combine_preprocess` hands the reduce-scatter the expected dtype and returns the activation dtype.
  - `TestCombineReduceInActivationDtype` (GPU, 8 ranks, TP2 x EP4, `NCCL_ALGO=Ring`): runs dispatch/combine through two MoE layers with identical weights, flag off and flag on. Each expert-TP rank gets a different bf16 partial result, and the test asserts that the combined outputs are `torch.equal`.
- Ran locally on CPU: `pytest tests/unit_tests/transformer/moe/test_combine_reduce_dtype.py`. Result: 17 passed, 1 skipped (the 8-rank GPU test).
- The GPU test has not been run on this branch. It needs an 8-GPU `torchrun` in CI.
- black, isort, ruff, and pylint run on the changed files: clean.

files.patch:
@@ -555,6 +555,7 @@ For MoE models, certain configurations may prevent CUDA Graph capture of MoE lay
 | --moe-pad-expert-input-to-capacity | Pad to capacity | False |
 | --moe-token-drop-policy | Drop policy: probs, position | probs |
 | --moe-permute-fusion | Fuse permutation ops | False |
+| --moe-combine-reduce-in-activation-dtype | alltoall with expert-TP size 2: reduce-scatter the combine in the activation dtype instead of the router dtype (bit-identical under NCCL Ring/PAT) | False |
 
 ### Performance Optimization
 | Argument | Description | Default |

@@ -67,6 +67,15 @@
 _HYBRIDEP_INT16_EXPERT_LIMIT = 1 << 15
 
 
+def _nccl_algo_may_use_nvls() -> bool:
+    """Returns whether ``NCCL_ALGO`` asks for NVLS.
+
+    Matches values such as ``NVLS`` or ``reducescatter:nvls``, but not the exclusion ``^NVLS``.
+    """
+    algo = os.environ.get("NCCL_ALGO", "").lower()
+    return "nvls" in algo and not algo.startswith("^")
+
+
 class MoETokenDispatcher:
     """
     MoE Token Dispatcher
@@ -799,6 +808,33 @@ def dispatch_postprocess(self, global_input_tokens, global_probs):
         self.tokens_per_expert = None
         return global_input_tokens, tokens_per_expert, global_probs
 
+    def _tp_reduce_dtype(self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor) -> torch.dtype:
+        """Returns the dtype for the expert-TP Reduce-Scatter in ``combine_preprocess``.
+
+        By default the expert outputs are upcast to the router probs dtype (e.g. FP32 with
+        ``moe_router_dtype='fp32'``), which avoids repeated low-precision roundings when the
+        expert-TP group has more than two ranks. With exactly two ranks the reduction is a
+        single addition per element, which NCCL's Ring and PAT kernels accumulate in FP32 and
+        round once, so the result equals the FP32 sum cast back to the activation dtype and the
+        upcast only costs an FP32 copy of every token-expert row. When
+        ``moe_combine_reduce_in_activation_dtype`` is set, the upcast is skipped for 2-rank
+        groups. NVLS reduces inside the NVSwitch and rounds differently, so the upcast is kept
+        whenever ``NCCL_ALGO`` asks for NVLS.
+
+        Args:
+            hidden_states (torch.Tensor): Expert outputs about to be reduce-scattered.
+
+        Returns:
+            torch.dtype: The dtype to reduce-scatter in.
+        """
+        if (
+            self.config.moe_combine_reduce_in_activation_dtype
+            and self.tp_size == 2
+            and not _nccl_algo_may_use_nvls()
+        ):
+            return hidden_states.dtype
+        return self.probs.dtype
+
     def combine_preprocess(self, hidden_states):
         """Prepares hidden states for token combination after expert computations.
 
@@ -833,7 +869,7 @@ def combine_preprocess(self, hidden_states):
             else:
                 input_split_sizes = self.output_splits_tp.tolist()
             hidden_states = reduce_scatter_to_sequence_parallel_region(
-                hidden_states.to(self.probs.dtype),
+                hidden_states.to(self._tp_reduce_dtype(hidden_states)),
                 group=self.tp_group,
                 input_split_sizes=input_split_sizes,
             ).to(hidden_states.dtype)

@@ -1074,6 +1074,14 @@ class TransformerConfig(ModelParallelConfig):
     moe_permute_fusion: bool = False
     """Fuse token rearrangement ops during token dispatching."""
 
+    moe_combine_reduce_in_activation_dtype: bool = False
+    """With the alltoall token dispatcher and an expert tensor parallel size of exactly 2, run
+    the expert-TP Reduce-Scatter in the token combine in the activation dtype (e.g. bf16) instead
+    of upcasting to the router probs dtype. With two ranks the reduction is one addition, which
+    NCCL's Ring and PAT kernels accumulate in FP32 and round once, so the result is bit-identical
+    to the FP32 path while sending half the bytes and skipping the FP32 copy of every
+    token-expert row. Ignored for other expert-TP sizes and when ``NCCL_ALGO`` asks for NVLS."""
+
     moe_router_fusion: bool = False
     """Enable fusion for MoE TopK routing and aux-loss computation. This is only
     supported in TransformerEngine 2.7.0 and above.

@@ -0,0 +1,148 @@
+# Copyright (c) 2026, NVIDIA CORPORATION. All rights reserved.
+
+"""Tests for the dtype of the expert-TP Reduce-Scatter in the alltoall token combine."""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+import megatron.core.transformer.moe.token_dispatcher as token_dispatcher
+from megatron.core.transformer.moe.token_dispatcher import MoEAlltoAllTokenDispatcher
+from megatron.core.typed_torch import apply_module
+from tests.unit_tests.test_utilities import Utils
+from tests.unit_tests.transformer.moe.test_token_dispatcher import (
+    MoEModelTestContainer,
+    token_permutation,
+    token_unpermutation,
+)
+
+
+def _make_dispatcher(tp_size, enabled, probs_dtype=torch.float32):
+    """Builds a dispatcher with only the attributes ``combine_preprocess`` reads."""
+    dispatcher = MoEAlltoAllTokenDispatcher.__new__(MoEAlltoAllTokenDispatcher)
+    dispatcher.config = SimpleNamespace(
+        moe_combine_reduce_in_activation_dtype=enabled, moe_permute_fusion=False
+    )
+    dispatcher.tp_size = tp_size
+    dispatcher.tp_group = None
+    dispatcher.num_local_experts = 1
+    dispatcher.output_splits_tp = None
+    dispatcher.probs = torch.zeros(1, dtype=probs_dtype)
+    return dispatcher
+
+
+class TestTpReduceDtype:
+    """CPU tests for ``MoEAlltoAllTokenDispatcher._tp_reduce_dtype``."""
+
+    @pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+    def _clear_nccl_algo(self, monkeypatch):
+        monkeypatch.delenv("NCCL_ALGO", raising=False)
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("tp_size", [2, 4, 8])
+    def test_disabled_keeps_probs_dtype(self, tp_size):
+        dispatcher = _make_dispatcher(tp_size, enabled=False)
+        hidden = torch.zeros(4, 8, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        assert dispatcher._tp_reduce_dtype(hidden) == torch.float32
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("activation_dtype", [torch.bfloat16, torch.float16])
+    def test_enabled_two_ranks_uses_activation_dtype(self, activation_dtype):
+        dispatcher = _make_dispatcher(2, enabled=True)
+        hidden = torch.zeros(4, 8, dtype=activation_dtype)
+        assert dispatcher._tp_reduce_dtype(hidden) == activation_dtype
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("tp_size", [4, 8])
+    def test_enabled_more_than_two_ranks_keeps_probs_dtype(self, tp_size):
+        dispatcher = _make_dispatcher(tp_size, enabled=True)
+        hidden = torch.zeros(4, 8, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        assert dispatcher._tp_reduce_dtype(hidden) == torch.float32
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
+        "nccl_algo,expected",
+        [
+            ("NVLS", torch.float32),
+            ("nvls", torch.float32),
+            ("Ring,NVLS", torch.float32),
+            ("reducescatter:nvls", torch.float32),
+            ("^NVLS", torch.bfloat16),
+            ("Ring", torch.bfloat16),
+            ("PAT", torch.bfloat16),
+        ],
+    )
+    def test_enabled_two_ranks_respects_nccl_algo(self, monkeypatch, nccl_algo, expected):
+        monkeypatch.setenv("NCCL_ALGO", nccl_algo)
+        dispatcher = _make_dispatcher(2, enabled=True)
+        hidden = torch.zeros(4, 8, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        assert dispatcher._tp_reduce_dtype(hidden) == expected
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
+        "tp_size,enabled,expected_reduce_dtype",
+        [(2, False, torch.float32), (2, True, torch.bfloat16), (4, True, torch.float32)],
+    )
+    def test_combine_preprocess_reduce_scatter_dtype(
+        self, monkeypatch, tp_size, enabled, expected_reduce_dtype
+    ):
+        seen = {}
+
+        def fake_reduce_scatter(input_, group=None, input_split_sizes=None):
+            seen["dtype"] = input_.dtype
+            return input_.clone()
+
+        monkeypatch.setattr(
+            token_dispatcher, "reduce_scatter_to_sequence_parallel_region", fake_reduce_scatter
+        )
+        dispatcher = _make_dispatcher(tp_size, enabled=enabled)
+        hidden = torch.randn(4, 8).to(torch.bfloat16)
+        out = dispatcher.combine_preprocess(hidden)
+        assert seen["dtype"] == expected_reduce_dtype
+        assert out.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        assert torch.equal(out, hidden)
+
+
+class TestCombineReduceInActivationDtype:
+    """Checks that the 2-rank bf16 reduce-scatter matches the FP32 path bit for bit."""
+
+    def teardown_method(self, method):
+        Utils.destroy_model_parallel()
+
+    @pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="CUDA not available")
+    @pytest.mark.skipif(Utils.world_size % 8 != 0, reason="needs a multiple of 8 ranks")
+    @pytest.mark.internal
+    @pytest.mark.timeout(120)
+    def test_two_rank_expert_tp_matches_fp32_reduce(self, monkeypatch):
+        monkeypatch.setenv("NCCL_ALGO", "Ring")
+        container = MoEModelTestContainer(
+            tp_size=2,
+            ep_size=4,
+            pp_size=1,
+            num_moe_experts=8,
+            moe_router_topk=2,
+            moe_router_load_balancing_type="aux_loss",
+            moe_token_dispatcher_type="alltoall",
+        )
+        reference_layer = container.moe_layer
+        bf16_layer = container.new_moe_layer(moe_combine_reduce_in_activation_dtype=True)
+        tp_rank = reference_layer.token_dispatcher.tp_rank
+
+        torch.manual_seed(1234)
+        hidden_states = torch.randn((32, 8, reference_layer.config.hidden_size), device="cuda")
+        probs, indices = apply_module(reference_layer.router)(hidden_states)
+
+        def combine(layer):
+            dispatcher = layer.token_dispatcher
+            permuted, _, permuted_probs = token_permutation(
+                dispatcher, hidden_states, probs, indices
+            )
+            # Give each expert-TP rank a different partial result so the reduction adds two
+            # distinct bf16 values, as the second expert-TP shard of a real expert would.
+            permuted = (
+                permuted.float() * permuted_probs.unsqueeze(-1) * (1.0 + 0.37 * tp_rank)
+            ).to(torch.bfloat16)
+            restored, _ = token_unpermutation(dispatcher, permuted)
+            return restored
+
+        with torch.no_grad():
+            expected = combine(reference_layer)
+            actual = combine(bf16_layer)
+        assert actual.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        assert torch.equal(actual, expected)
